headline: Alignment-free k-mers separate pre- and post-Omicron Delta spike sequences
label: Viral Genomic Evolution Surveillance
summary: Sequence-based methods now resolve variant lineages from wastewater mixtures and track viral evolution within immunocompromised hosts.
synthesis: The dominant thread is genomic tracking of SARS-CoV-2 evolution across scales, from lineage-level sequence composition to within-host and environmental populations. An alignment-free k-mer random forest reaches 93% accuracy in separating pre- and post-Omicron Delta spike sequences and identifies persistent mutations, offering a lineage-discrimination route that does not depend on alignment. A wastewater study applies fused ridge temporal regularization with bootstrapping to deconvolve variant abundances from mixed sequencing time series. Another study examines viral evolution during primary infection in immunocompromised hosts. A macrophage study addresses the host temporal response to spike proteins under circadian immunometabolic states and is less directly genomic. What is new is the combination of composition-based classification with population-level deconvolution of variant mixtures.
